title: Canonical etale derived adjunction on ordinary chain transposes
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ any commutative ring. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on small etale sites and the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $r_R^*\dashv r_{*,R}$ for the exact module inverse-image adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $Q$ be localization and let $\alpha_K:Q(r_{*,R}K)\to Rr_{*,R}(QK)$ be the canonical right-derived comparison, defined using K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived].

There is a canonical derived adjunction $r_R^*\dashv Rr_{*,R}$, with $r_R^*$ represented termwise [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For any cochain complexes $M$ on $V$ and $K$ on $W$, and any chain map $f:M\to r_{*,R}K$, its Hom bijection satisfies
$$e_R(\alpha_K\circ Qf)=Q(f^\flat),\qquad f^\flat=\varepsilon^0_K\circ r_R^*f:r_R^*M\to K,$$
where the right side uses the canonical exact-pullback identification $r_R^*(QM)\cong Q(r_R^*M)$. The maps $\alpha_K$ and this formula are natural in chain maps in both variables. In particular, setting $M=r_{*,R}K$ and $f=1$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{QK}\circ r_R^*(\alpha_K)=Q(\varepsilon^0_K).$$
No boundedness, acyclicity, flatness or properness assumption is required.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod(W_{\Et},R)$, $L=r_R^*$ and $G=r_{*,R}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), we have $L\dashv G$ with $L$ additive and exact; $G$ is additive because its stated sectionwise formula preserves sums of module maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](a),(b), they give adjunctions on complexes and on homotopy categories, with transpose $f\mapsto\varepsilon^0_K\circ Lf$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $L$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends termwise to $D(L)$, with the natural identification $D(L)(QM)\cong Q(LM)$. In all subsequent equations this identification is understood.

source.place: Tags 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, termwise adjunction) and 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC

proof.text: Use small representatives of the sites in a containing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], every complex of $\mathcal B$ admits a K-injective resolution. The functor $QG:K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A)$ is exact: $G$ is additive, so it preserves the finite biproduct and differential matrix defining each cone, including its minus sign, and it commutes termwise with shifts; the cone triangulation of the homotopy category and exactness of its localization are stated by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], with cone matrices as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] applies and gives the canonical pair $(RG,\alpha)$, with $\alpha_I:Q(GI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(QI)$ for every K-injective $I$. This is the pair called $Rr_{*,R}$ and $\alpha$ in the statement.

source.place: Tags 014X (lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category) and 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); sites-cohomology.tex Section 07A5; injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text: Choose a resolution $j:K\to I$ as above. Since $L$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $GI$ K-injective in $\mathcal A$. Set $c_j=\alpha_I^{-1}\circ RG(Qj):RG(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(GI)$. The comparison calculation of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] identifies this isomorphism with the canonical computation on $I$. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives the particular equality $c_j\circ\alpha_K=Q(Gj)$. No claim that $G$ preserves the quasi-isomorphism $j$ is used: $RG(Qj)$ is invertible because $Qj$ is.

For every complex $M$ compose the bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(QM,RG(QK))
&\xrightarrow{c_j\circ-}\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(QM,Q(GI))\\
&\xrightarrow{Q^{-1}}\Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(M,GI)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{adj}}\Hom_{K(\mathcal B)}(LM,I)\\
&\xrightarrow{Q}\Hom_{D(\mathcal B)}(Q(LM),QI)
\xrightarrow{(Qj)^{-1}\circ-}\Hom_{D(\mathcal B)}(Q(LM),QK).
\end{aligned}$$
Both uses of $Q$ on Hom sets are bijections by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], since $GI$ and $I$ are K-injective; the middle bijection is [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](b). Denote the resulting bijection by $e_{M,K}$.

For a derived arrow $h:QK\to QK'$, choose resolutions $j:K\to I$, $j':K'\to I'$. By [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], it is represented by a unique homotopy class $g:I\to I'$ and satisfies
$$Qg\circ Qj=Qj'\circ h,\qquad c_{j'}RG(h)=Q(Gg)c_j.$$
For $a:QM\to RG(QK)$, let $t:M\to GI$ represent $c_ja$. Then $Gg\circ t$ represents $c_{j'}RG(h)a$. By naturality of the homotopy adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], its transpose is $g\circ t^\flat$. Hence
$$e_{M,K'}(RG(h)a)=(Qj')^{-1}Qg\,Q(t^\flat)=h\,e_{M,K}(a).$$
Taking $h=1$ and two resolutions of the same $K$ proves independence of the resolution. Precomposing by a chain map $b:M'\to M$ gives $e_{M',K}(a\,Qb)=e_{M,K}(a)Q(Lb)$ by the same homotopy-adjunction naturality. These equalities descend uniquely to all derived source arrows by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), applied to the two Hom functors on the opposite source category: both invert quasi-isomorphisms, since $L$ does. Thus $e$ is bifunctorial on the derived categories.

source.place: Tags 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), functoriality in both variables

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to $e^{-1}$. It gives $D(L)\dashv RG$, whose inverse Hom bijection is $e$. Its construction is precisely the canonical K-injective derived adjunction: the Hom calculation of Step 4 uses the given comparison isomorphisms $c_j$, and Step 5 proves independence of their resolution choices. For a chain map $f:M\to GK$, Step 3 gives
$$c_j(\alpha_K\circ Qf)=Q(Gj\circ f).$$
Thus Step 4 represents this morphism by $Gj\circ f$, whose ordinary transpose is
$$\varepsilon^0_I\circ L(Gj\circ f)=j\circ\varepsilon^0_K\circ Lf=j\circ f^\flat$$
by the natural counit in [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](a). The last arrow of Step 4 cancels $Qj$ and yields $e_{M,K}(\alpha_K\circ Qf)=Q(f^\flat)$. This proves the required formula for arbitrary complexes, without resolving $M$.

source.place: Tag 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility), counit square; Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with derived.tex Tags 0FND/070I

proof.text:
For chain maps $b:M'\to M$ and $k:K\to K'$, the ordinary transpose satisfies
$$(Gk\circ f\circ b)^\flat=k\circ f^\flat\circ Lb.$$
This is the naturality assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Together with $\alpha_{K'}Q(Gk)=RG(Qk)\alpha_K$ and the bifunctoriality of Step 5, it proves naturality of the displayed formula in both variables. Finally put $M=GK$, $f=1_{GK}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], $e(a)=\varepsilon_{QK}\circ D(L)(a)$. The formula is therefore exactly $\varepsilon_{QK}\circ D(L)(\alpha_K)=Q(\varepsilon^0_K)$. All resolutions above were unbounded resolutions of arbitrary module-sheaf complexes, and the sole exactness hypothesis used was that of constant-coefficient $L$.
